changes_vs_current: New topic. Scope: one item per airline brand. American Eagle (YouGov fame 68%) is left out because it is American's regional brand and people fold it into 'American'. Defunct airlines are kept only with data. Spirit stays: it shut down May 2, 2026, but YouGov still shows 89% fame and it was in the BTS and Statista data until then. Virgin America (YouGov page 71%, defunct since 2018), Pan Am (Wikipedia #9 only), TWA, Ryanair (no US YouGov page; global Wikipedia #4 only), Breeze, Sun Country (fame 43%), Japan Airlines (59%) and Norwegian (58%) are left off. Computed order: average position over 5 people sources (YouGov fame, BTS share, Statista bookings, YouGov consideration, Wikipedia pageviews), missing = list length + 5. Result: 1 Delta 1.6, 2 American 2.2, 3 United 3.0, 4 Southwest 5.9, 5 Alaska 7.9, 6 JetBlue 9.1, 7 Spirit 9.4, 8 Air Canada 10.3, 9 British Airways 10.7, 10 Emirates 11.1, 11 Lufthansa 11.4, 12 Qatar 11.6, 13 Frontier 12.1, 14 Etihad 13.8, 15 Cathay 13.8, 16 Qantas 14.0, 17 Virgin Atlantic 14.1, 18 Singapore 14.2, 19 Ryanair 14.2, 20 Air France 14.8, 21 Hawaiian 14.8, 22 Korean 14.9, 23 Turkish 15.0, 24 KLM 15.2, 25 Pan Am 15.2, 26 Allegiant 15.7, 27 JAL 16.6. Gut-check moves: (1) Frontier 13 -> 8. It is #7 in BTS domestic share and 82% YouGov fame (tied with British Airways for 8th). Only the global Wikipedia count puts it low (#23). (2) Hawaiian 21 -> 11. YouGov US popularity puts it 9th (39%), above every overseas carrier except British Airways and Air Canada, and its fame (70%) is above Virgin Atlantic, Lufthansa and Emirates. It drops out of BTS only because its traffic is now reported under Alaska after the merger, and its low Wikipedia count is global readership. (3) Allegiant 26 -> 12. YouGov fame 67% beats Lufthansa 66% and Emirates 62%, and its popularity (36%) beats every overseas carrier except British Airways and Air Canada. Again only global Wikipedia puts it low. (4) Emirates 10 -> 13, with Lufthansa 14 and Qatar 15. Emirates is in the gut check, but US YouGov puts it below Allegiant on both fame (62 vs 67) and popularity (33 vs 36). Its 10th place came from Wikipedia (#3), where Gulf, Indian and European readership inflates it. (5) Air Canada stays above British Airways (9 vs 10) as computed: it is in Statista's US top 8 booked and has higher popularity (45 vs 40). British Airways has higher fame (82 vs 79). (6) Tail 16-24: Etihad and Cathay (computed 14-15) move to 23-24. Their US YouGov fame is the lowest of any candidate (42%, 40%), and only global Wikipedia lifts them. Air France (75% US fame, 11th) moves up to 16 because its low English-Wikipedia count (#28) reflects French readers using French Wikipedia. The rest keep the computed order with US fame breaking ties: Virgin Atlantic 17, Singapore 18, Qantas 19, Korean Air 20, KLM 21, Turkish 22. Alaska is above JetBlue as computed (BTS 7.1% vs 4.6%, Wikipedia 12 vs 18). JetBlue leads only on fame (85 vs 84).
confidence: High for 1-4 (every source agrees, with Delta/American/United in some order, then Southwest). Medium-high for 5-8 (Alaska, JetBlue, Spirit and Frontier are the obvious next tier; Spirit's defunct status may lower how often people name it). Medium for 9-15: the order of overseas carriers versus Hawaiian and Allegiant rests on YouGov US fame and popularity plus the gut check, because no US 'name an airline' poll exists. Medium-low for 16-24: these rest mainly on YouGov fame and global Wikipedia pageviews. Caveats: the only open-recall poll found (PPP 2013) is old and used a closed list. J.D. Power gives satisfaction, not salience. The YouGov consideration report's full data is behind a download (only the top 4 were read, via Islands). Google Trends was not accessible.
